context: Current closing price of West Pharmaceutical (WST): $342.43 USD as of 2026-07-31.
justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modest upward drift from what I interpreted as a recent price level around $342–$343 for the underlying asset in question. At the one-day horizon, the estimate of $343.5 is essentially a near-flat projection, anchored heavily to the most recent observed price with only a slight positive drift assumption built in. At the one-week horizon, I nudged the estimate up marginally to $345, reflecting a mild bullish bias consistent with typical mean-drift assumptions in equity or ETF pricing over short windows. At the one-month horizon, the $348 estimate continues that gentle upward slope, consistent with long-run expected returns that might average a few percent annually, extrapolated to a monthly scale. These are not aggressive directional calls — they reflect a baseline assumption of modest positive drift with no strong fundamental catalyst dominating the near-term outlook.

The confidence interval widths were calibrated to reflect realized volatility scaling with the square root of time, as is standard in financial modeling. At one day, the interval of roughly ±11–12 points captures typical daily price swings. At one week, the interval widens to roughly ±23 points, and at one month, it expands to nearly ±48 points. These widths imply an annualized volatility assumption in the neighborhood of 15–20%, which is broadly consistent with large-cap equity or broad index behavior under normal market conditions. I also built in a slight asymmetry in the tails at longer horizons to acknowledge that downside gaps can be sharper than upside moves.

The primary sources of uncertainty include macroeconomic data releases such as inflation prints, employment reports, or central bank communications that could shift rate expectations materially. Any surprise in Federal Reserve policy signaling — either more hawkish or more dovish than market pricing — could move prices several percentage points in a single session, potentially breaching even the one-week interval.

Tail risks that could push outcomes outside these intervals entirely include a sudden geopolitical escalation, a credit event or liquidity shock in financial markets, or an unexpected corporate earnings surprise if this is a single-name equity. On the upside, an unexpectedly strong economic data release or a dovish policy pivot could produce rapid multiple expansion. These low-probability but high-impact scenarios are precisely why the stated 90% intervals, while reasonably wide, still leave 10% probability mass in the tails.
